objective: Prepare a candidate entry for the sixth High-Lift Prediction Workshop test case 1 by running the published CRM-HLS blind case on the coarsest committee grid of 2.66 million cells across the six specified angles of attack, and assess whether the result is strong enough to be worth Katie approving an approach to the workshop organisers
rationale: This is the strongest externally verified credential currently open to this lab, and the scouting sweep of 2026-07-30 found it by looking. The workshop is underway as of January 2026 with the meeting expected June 2027, its submission repository is already public, and its participant list is full of companies including Boeing, Embraer, ONERA, DLR, JAXA and Bombardier, so a commercial entrant is normal rather than exceptional. Membership of the sponsoring society is not required. Decisively for us, the coarsest published grid is 2.66 million cells, which is under five times our largest ever converged primal, and the case is deliberately blind with no experimental data published, so there is nothing to tune toward and placing well cannot be an artifact of hindsight. A workshop entry that is externally rescored is worth more to this company than another internal case
citations: Sixth AIAA High-Lift Prediction Workshop, test case 1, CRM high lift simplified configuration, specification version 1.0 of January 2026
High-Lift Prediction Workshop 6 grid statistics for the HeldenMesh family, coarsest level 2661338 cells

cost_basis: Measured on this machine on 2026-08-01, replacing the earlier estimate. The coarsest committee grid was downloaded, imported, decomposed and solved here. It parses to exactly 2661338 cells, 1156796 nodes and 6509759 faces, all prisms, pyramids and tetrahedra, which confirms the cited cell count against the grid file itself. Peak memory across every stage was 4548 MiB against 31380 MiB of host memory, a headroom factor of 6.7, so the memory question the earlier basis left open is answered and memory was never the risk. The per cell figure comes from a measured slope over a four rung ladder at 334647, 673920, 1320300 and 2664180 cells rather than from one point, and it over predicts the real grid by 11 percent because a structured mesh carries more faces per cell, so it is a bound in the safe direction. Throughput measured at 120 iterations in 182.63 seconds on 14 ranks, which is 0.355 core minutes per iteration, 2.02 times the rate the earlier basis assumed. The cause is rank count and grid type, not cell count: rung A6 ran 4 ranks on a structured extruded mesh and parallel efficiency here is about 45 percent, so 14 ranks buys 6.3 times the wall speed for 2.23 times the core minutes. Carrying the earlier assumption of 3000 iterations across the six angles gives 6390 core minutes at 14 ranks, or 4014 serial over 67 hours of wall time. Two things remain unpriced and are stated rather than hidden. The iteration count is still an assumption, which is the same defect that overran the flat plate finest rung, and at the upper angles steady RANS often refuses to settle. And the configuration measured as stable uses first order convection, which is not a defensible submission; a second order entry is dearer and less robust. What actually blocks this item is not memory but numerics on a grid built for node centred codes, with 1256565 severely non orthogonal faces, plus the fact that no reader for the published grid format existed here until one was written.
expected_knowledge_gain: The first externally rescored aerodynamic result this lab would ever hold, on a blind case, judged beside national laboratories and airframers. Even a mediocre placement establishes that our pipeline runs a modern high lift configuration end to end at several million cells, which no current record demonstrates. A failure is nearly as informative, since it would locate our ceiling against a published grid rather than against our own guess
launch_prompt: Prepare, do not send. Download the sixth High-Lift Prediction Workshop test case 1 specification and the coarsest published grid of the HeldenMesh family, 2661338 cells, from the public grid store. FIRST run a memory probe at a single angle of attack and report peak resident set size before queueing anything else; this grid is 4.6 times our largest ever converged primal and the memory envelope at that size is not established. If the probe fits, run the six specified angles of attack from 10 to 35 degrees at the published conditions of Mach 0.20 and chord Reynolds number 3.55 million, free air with no tunnel or support hardware. Produce the required outputs, which are surface streamlines, skin friction magnitude contours (magnitude, not the x component), and pressure and skin friction along the defined rows. Report every deviation from the specification plainly. ABSOLUTE: do not contact the workshop organisers, do not join a technology focus group distribution list, do not request a participant identifier, do not open a merge request against the submission repository, and do not create any account. Katie decides whether this lab approaches this workshop at all, and she proofreads anything that would be sent. The deliverable here is a result plus an honest assessment of whether it is worth her approving that approach.
cost_basis_previous: Estimate, anchored on our own measured throughput and deliberately conservative. Rung A6 converged 579072 cells in 38.4 core-min for 1000 iterations, which is 6.6e-5 core-min per cell per 1000 iterations. The coarsest workshop grid is 2661338 cells, so one angle of attack at 3000 iterations scales to about 530 core-min, and the six specified angles to about 3200 core-min. Rounded to 3600 to allow for a high-lift case needing more iterations to settle than a cruise wing does. This is the largest single compute request on the docket and it is a real commitment, not a screen. Memory is the genuine risk and is not established: A6 held 30 GB free at 579072 cells but this grid is 4.6 times larger, so the first action must be a memory probe on a single angle before the remaining five are queued. Dollars: zero for the grids, which are anonymous public downloads. Any attendance fee is a separate decision and is not established for this edition
repriced_note: Repriced 2026-08-01 from a direct measurement on the real committee grid: it runs on this machine at 4.55 GiB of 30.6, so memory was never the risk. Two agents probed this item independently and reached the same measured rate; the 14-rank figure of 6,390 core-min is kept. Evidence and method: the hlpw6 directory under the site root. Submission mechanics, which no compute number covers, are recorded there in the submission gate note.
